home-remodeling.meta_description: 1960s canal ranches in Lighthouse Point stripped and rebuilt for how you live now, permitted through city and county. Call (786) 273-2524.
home-remodeling.hero_sub: Full-gut and whole-home remodeling for Lighthouse Point canal houses: layout changes, new mechanicals, and impact glass across the water elevation. Permitted through the city, supervised daily, built by a licensed general contractor, Lic. CGC1539072.
intro_paragraphs: Lighthouse Point is a city of about 2.4 square miles wrapped around roughly 18 miles of waterway, and the housing follows the water. Venetian Isles, Lighthouse Manor and Wooler Heights were added between 1957 and 1969, and Coral Key and Pompano Waterway Estates came into the city in 1970. Around eight in ten homes here are single family, and street after street of them are single-story ranches on wide canal lots with docks behind. Owners rarely want a different address. They want the same dock with a house that finally matches it, which is why whole-home remodeling is the local sport.

The City of Lighthouse Point Building and Zoning Department reviews and permits the work, and contractors have to be registered with the city, insurance certificate and all, before they can even apply. Above that sits a county layer most homeowners never meet: the Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals, which administers the Florida Building Code countywide, certifies the officials and inspectors who sign off on your job, and issues the formal interpretation when a code section is genuinely in dispute. Broward also sits inside the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, so windows, doors and roofing all need HVHZ product approvals. Canal lots bring FEMA flood elevations into the conversation as well.

Twenty years and then some of South Florida work back that up, plus 150-plus remodels and additions delivered, every one permitted and inspected. On a Lighthouse Point gut we work to a fixed written scope agreed before demolition, with a supervisor on site every working day and dust control that keeps the half of the house you are still using livable. Material deliveries get staged so your neighbor's driveway stays their driveway. One team and one phone number, from the first estimate through the warranty. Licensed and insured, Lic. CGC1539072.
home-remodeling.scope_intro: Nothing gets opened until there is a priced, written scope. Here is what a full remodel of a Lighthouse Point canal house normally covers.

scope_items.name: Walls out, glass in
scope_items.desc: Removing the interior walls that hid the canal, then rebuilding the rear elevation with HVHZ-approved impact glass and sliding systems sized to the view.

scope_items.name: The unglamorous replacements
scope_items.desc: New electrical service and panel, repiped supply and drain lines, and ductwork sized for a house that no longer has eight small rooms.

scope_items.name: Slab, tie beam and roof
scope_items.desc: Structural work these sixties builds tend to need: spalled slab edges, tie beam upgrades where new openings land, and roof framing brought to current uplift standards.

scope_items.name: Kitchen and baths on one permit
scope_items.desc: Both rooms carried on a single permit set and a single schedule, so the plumbing goes in once, the waterproofing is signed off before stone covers it, and the house is opened up only one time.

scope_items.name: Finishes chosen for salt air
scope_items.desc: Hardware, hinges, exterior fixtures and railings specified for a house that sits fifty feet from brackish water and gets the sea breeze daily.

faqs.q: Does my contractor have to be registered with the City of Lighthouse Point?
faqs.a: Yes. The city requires contractors to register with the Building and Zoning Department before they can pull a permit, which means state license, workers' compensation coverage or exemption, and a general liability certificate made out to the City of Lighthouse Point on file. It is a small administrative gate that quietly filters out a lot of trouble. We handle our own registration and the permit applications, so you are not chasing paperwork for your own remodel.

faqs.q: Does the county Board of Rules and Appeals touch a city permit?
faqs.a: It shapes the permit without ever touching it. The Board of Rules and Appeals administers the Florida Building Code across the county, certifies the building officials and inspectors who work in it, hears appeals of their decisions, and issues formal interpretations when a code section is truly in dispute. Day to day, your permit still lives with the Lighthouse Point building department. The practical effect is a consistent countywide standard and a place to settle a disagreement.

faqs.q: Our house is from 1963. Gut it or tear it down?
faqs.a: That depends on the shell, and it is worth deciding with an engineer rather than a feeling. If the block walls, tie beam and foundation are sound and the footprint suits you, a gut buys you a new house inside an existing structure, usually with less permitting friction than a rebuild. If the ceilings are low, the floor sits below where you want it, and you are already replacing every system anyway, a rebuild can pencil out better. We will walk it and say which yours is.

faqs.q: Can we stay in the house while the work happens?
faqs.a: For a phased remodel, often yes. We can seal off a wing, keep one bathroom and a temporary kitchenette running, and protect the pathways between them. For a true full gut with ceilings open and the panel replaced, living there is miserable for you and slower for us, so most owners move out for the heavy months and return for finish work. That call gets made before demolition, not halfway through it.

faqs.q: What does a whole-home remodel run in Lighthouse Point?
faqs.a: Wide range, and anyone quoting a number before walking the house is guessing. A finishes-and-kitchen refresh is one budget; a full gut with new service, new mechanicals, structural openings and impact glass across the water elevation is another entirely. What we commit to is a fixed written scope with real allowances instead of a low opener that grows by change order. PGX is a high-end contractor and usually not the cheapest bid on the table.

home-remodeling.cta_sub: Bring the survey if you have one and the list of what annoys you. We price it, write it down, and stand behind the number, in English o en español.

kitchen-remodeling.title: Kitchen Remodeling in Lighthouse Point FL | PGX Builders
kitchen-remodeling.meta_description: Lighthouse Point kitchen remodeling that finally faces the canal, with humidity-rated cabinetry and city permits pulled. (786) 273-2524.
kitchen-remodeling.hero_sub: Custom cabinetry, stone counters and structural openings for Lighthouse Point kitchens that were built facing the wrong way. Permitted by discipline through the city building department and supervised on site every working day.
kitchen-remodeling.local_heading: The kitchen that never saw the canal
intro_paragraphs: The mid-century builders who filled Venetian Isles and Coral Key Villas put the kitchen where the plumbing was cheapest: usually toward the street, walled off from the family room, and blind to the water the whole lot was sold for. Sixty years later that is the single most common complaint we hear in Lighthouse Point. A kitchen remodel here is really a reorientation. Take out the wall to the Florida room, move the range off the exterior wall, and put the sink and the island where somebody can watch a boat come up the canal while dinner cooks.

A serious kitchen touches plumbing, gas, electrical and often structure, so it is permitted work through the Lighthouse Point Building and Zoning Department, with a separate application for each discipline and inspections along the way. Painting and tile need no permit; nearly everything else in a kitchen does. If the scope enlarges a window or cuts a new opening to the terrace, the replacement unit needs an HVHZ product approval, because Broward County sits inside the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone alongside Miami-Dade. And a sixties panel often needs upgrading before an induction range and a wine room become realistic.

The sequence is what protects a kitchen. Cabinets are ordered early and stored dry, stone is templated after the boxes are set rather than off a drawing, and appliance specifications are locked before a single rough-in gets cut. A supervisor is on site daily, floors and the route from your front door are protected, and the site is swept before anyone leaves. Twenty-plus years in South Florida, 150-plus remodels and additions, all of it permitted and inspected. Lic. CGC1539072.
kitchen-remodeling.scope_heading: How the canal kitchen gets built
kitchen-remodeling.scope_intro: Every kitchen gets specified line by line before demolition, from hinge to hood. Below is what usually lands in a canal-front floor plan.

scope_items.desc: Removing the partition between kitchen and Florida room with an engineered beam and a permit, so the cook finally gets the canal view.

scope_items.desc: Natural stone or porcelain templated once the boxes are level, with island structure engineered for seating overhangs rather than trusted to a fabricator's optimism.

scope_items.desc: Relocating ranges, hoods and refrigeration where the new layout wants them, with gas lines, dedicated circuits and exterior venting permitted and inspected.

scope_items.name: Panel, circuits and light
scope_items.desc: Service upgrades where a sixties panel cannot carry the appliance package, plus layered lighting that works at six in the morning and at a dinner party.

faqs.q: Which parts of a kitchen project actually need a permit here?
faqs.a: The city lists painting, carpet and tile as work you can do without one. Everything else in a real kitchen is permitted work: plumbing moves, gas, electrical, structural openings, new windows or doors, exterior venting, each applied for by discipline and inspected before it gets covered. Skipping that step earns a stop work order and a penalty set at twice the original fee, which is an expensive way to save a week.

faqs.q: Can we open the kitchen wall in a 1960s block house?
faqs.a: Usually. These houses are concrete block with a poured tie beam, and interior partitions are frequently non-bearing, which makes the opening straightforward. Where the wall carries roof load, an engineer sizes a beam and the sealed calculations go in with the permit set. What we will not do is cut first and calculate afterward. We get the structural answer before you commit to a layout, so the drawing you fall in love with is the one we actually build.

faqs.q: How long from signing to the first dinner in the new kitchen?
faqs.a: Cabinetry sets the clock. Custom packages take months to fabricate, so we order early and hold demolition until the schedule says go, rather than leaving you cooking in the garage while a shop catches up. On-site work for a full kitchen typically runs a couple of months, longer with structural openings, a service upgrade or a relocated gas line. Think in seasons, not weekends, and plan the holidays around it.

faqs.q: We are on a canal. Does that change the kitchen at all?
faqs.a: It changes the specification more than the process. Salt-laden air is hard on hinges, pulls, faucet finishes and unprotected steel, so we lean on marine-grade and properly coated hardware. If the scope enlarges a window on the water elevation, that unit needs an HVHZ approval and the opening gets flashed properly rather than caulked and hoped over. A pass-through window to the summer kitchen is a very Lighthouse Point request and an easy one to detail correctly.

faqs.q: Why is a high-end kitchen so far above a showroom quote?
faqs.a: Because most of the money sits in things a showroom price never includes: custom cabinetry, natural stone, a panel that can carry the appliances, a beam where a wall used to be, and permitted rough-ins that pass inspection. We scope it in writing after walking your house, so you are comparing a specification rather than a per-foot guess. If price is the only variable that matters, we will say so early and part on friendly terms.

kitchen-remodeling.cta_sub: Fifteen minutes in your kitchen and we can tell you what is possible, then a written scope and a fixed number, in English o en español.

bathroom-remodeling.title: Lighthouse Point Bathroom Remodels, FL | PGX Builders
bathroom-remodeling.meta_description: Lighthouse Point bath remodels replace sixties supply lines, then tile over a membrane we flood-test first. Licensed GC at (786) 273-2524.
bathroom-remodeling.hero_sub: Primary suites, frameless showers and freestanding tubs across Lighthouse Point, with flood-tested waterproofing and new supply lines behind the marble. Fully permitted, inspected, and run by a licensed and insured general contractor.
intro_paragraphs: Bathrooms are the first thing to date a Lighthouse Point house. The ranches through Lighthouse Manor, Wooler Heights and Coral Key Villas were built with two compact baths and a hall linen closet, which read as generous in 1964 and reads as nothing now. So owners combine a small fourth bedroom with the hall bath to make a genuine primary suite, or take a tired eighties renovation down to block and start over in stone. Guest baths get the same thinking on a smaller budget, because a house that hosts boat crowds needs one that actually works.

Bathroom work is permitted through the City of Lighthouse Point Building and Zoning Department, with separate plumbing, electrical and mechanical applications and inspections before anything gets closed up. The county layer matters too: Broward's Board of Rules and Appeals administers the code and certifies the inspectors who sign off on your rough plumbing. If you are in one of the city's townhome or low-rise condo pockets, add association approval and the Broward County Building Safety Inspection Program, which applies to older multi-family buildings while one and two family homes are exempt from it.

Optimism is not a waterproofing method. We flood-test shower pans before tile, slope to the drain by measurement rather than by eye, install blocking for heavy glass while the wall is still open, and vent the fan outside instead of into the attic where every shortcut eventually rots. Fixed written scope, daily supervision, and protected floors from your entry door to the work zone. Insured and licensed under CGC1539072, with 150-plus remodels and additions behind us, every one of them permitted and inspected.
bathroom-remodeling.scope_heading: Where the bath budget actually goes
bathroom-remodeling.scope_intro: Half of a good bathroom is invisible by the time you see it. Here is what we build into a Lighthouse Point primary or guest bath.

scope_items.name: Bedroom absorbed into suite
scope_items.desc: Turning a spare bedroom, closet and hall bath into one primary suite, with the layout and rough-ins settled on paper before anything comes down.

scope_items.name: A pan we flood-test
scope_items.desc: Waterproofing membrane installed to spec, then filled and left overnight to prove it, because the tile above it is not coming back up cheaply.

scope_items.name: Glass hung on real blocking
scope_items.desc: Frameless panels and heavy hinges anchored to blocking set while the wall was open, not to drywall anchors chosen on the last afternoon.

scope_items.name: Replacing the original supply
scope_items.desc: Swapping sixties galvanized and cast iron for modern drain and supply lines while the walls are open and the access costs you nothing extra.

scope_items.name: Ventilation and light that work
scope_items.desc: Fans specified for the duct run they actually have, vented outside, with vanity and shower lighting on separate switches instead of one glare doing all the work.

faqs.q: Is a permit really needed just to redo a bathroom?
faqs.a: For anything past paint and tile, yes. Moving or replacing plumbing, altering wiring, adding an exhaust fan or a heated floor all require permits from the Lighthouse Point building department, with inspections before the waterproofing and rough plumbing get hidden. Treat that sequence as a feature rather than a hurdle. It is documented proof that the parts you will never see again were done right, and it is exactly what a buyer's inspector goes looking for later.

faqs.q: Can I get a curbless shower in a slab-on-grade ranch?
faqs.a: Often, but the slab decides. Recessing the pan means cutting concrete and sometimes rerouting drain lines below, which is doable and not free. Where the drain run or slab thickness will not allow it, a low-profile curb with a correctly sloped pan and a linear drain gets you close to the same look. We check the plumbing layout before you commit to that detail, so nobody discovers the constraint after the demolition bin arrives.

faqs.q: Our primary bath faces the canal. Anything special about that?
faqs.a: Two things. Salt-laden air is unkind to plated fixtures and budget hardware, so we specify finishes and hinges that still look right in year five. And if the scope adds or enlarges a window on the water elevation, that opening needs an HVHZ-approved unit and proper flashing, since Broward County is inside the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone. Frosted impact glass above a freestanding tub is a request we get constantly here, and a straightforward one to detail.

faqs.q: How long are we without the bathroom?
faqs.a: A straightforward guest bath is typically a few weeks on site once the permit is in hand. A full primary suite that moves walls, replaces supply and drain lines and takes custom stone runs considerably longer, and the schedule usually waits on materials rather than labor. We order stone, glass and fixtures before demolition so the room is not sitting open and idle. If it is your only bathroom, we will tell you and phase the work.

faqs.q: Should we replace the old plumbing while the walls are open?
faqs.a: Almost always. Galvanized supply and cast iron drains from the early sixties are at the end of a normal service life, and a beautiful new bath tied into a failing stack is a bet with poor odds. Opening those walls again later costs several times what doing it now does. We scope camera inspections early so the decision rests on what the pipe actually looks like inside, not on a hunch.

bathroom-remodeling.cta_sub: Show us the room and your reference photos. We will tell you what the plumbing allows and put a real number on it, in English o en español.

home-additions.title: Home Additions for Lighthouse Point FL | PGX Builders
home-additions.meta_description: Lighthouse Point additions: rear extensions and second stories with seawall letters and engineering handled. Talk to PGX at (786) 273-2524.
home-additions.h1: Grow the house, keep the canal
home-additions.hero_sub: Rear extensions, second stories and garage conversions for Lighthouse Point homes: engineered, surveyed, and permitted through the city building department, including the seawall letters waterfront submittals require. Supervised daily by a licensed GC.
home-additions.local_heading: Where an addition meets a seawall
intro_paragraphs: Lighthouse Point lots are wide, flat and finite, and almost every one of them ends at a seawall. That geometry drives the additions built here: a rear great room and primary suite pushed toward the water in Venetian Isles, a second story over a low-slung ranch in Coral Key Harbor so the upstairs bedrooms can finally see the canal, a garage turned into a guest suite in Pompano Waterway Estates for the family that arrives by boat every winter. Nobody in this city wants to leave the water. They want more house between the street and the dock.

Additions are the most paperwork-intensive thing you can build in this city, and the Lighthouse Point Building and Zoning Department is specific about it. The single-family checklist wants sealed plans and structural calculations, three surveys with site plans showing setbacks, soil density tests, a separately filed drainage plan, product approvals signed by the designer of record, and, on waterfront property, three sealed engineer's letters confirming the seawall can carry the added upland improvements. Zoning adds geometry: anything above 28.5 feet steps back two more feet for every foot of height. Broward County environmental review stamps new-home plans first.

Tying new construction to a 1960s block house is where experience earns its keep. Footings have to meet existing footings, the new tie beam has to land somewhere real, and the stucco seam has to disappear or everyone will see it forever. We stage the work so the half of the house you still live in stays livable, keep the site tidy on a street where the neighbors are also your dock neighbors, and run a fixed written scope with a supervisor present daily. One accountable team from the feasibility conversation through final inspection and warranty.
home-additions.scope_heading: Space you can still add here
home-additions.scope_intro: An addition starts with an engineer and an honest read of what the existing structure can carry. Here are the five we are asked for most often.

scope_items.name: Rear wings facing the canal
scope_items.desc: Great rooms and primary suites run out to the rear setback line, with new footings, tie beam and roof joint solved on paper first.

scope_items.name: Second stories over a ranch
scope_items.desc: Structural evaluation of the existing block and footings first, then an upper floor designed inside the city's height and stepped-setback rules.

scope_items.name: Garages into guest suites
scope_items.desc: Converting garage or carport space into conditioned rooms, insulated and mechanically served, with the permit trail that makes it legal living area.

scope_items.name: Suites for family who stay
scope_items.desc: A private in-law wing with a full bath and small galley, permitted as living space and scaled to the house rather than looking bolted onto the side of it.

scope_items.name: Concrete, steel and connections
scope_items.desc: Underpinning, new footings, steel and tie beam upgrades: the half of an addition budget nobody sees and the half that decides its lifespan.

faqs.q: Why does an addition permit ask for a letter about my seawall?
faqs.a: Because the seawall is structure. On waterfront property, Lighthouse Point asks for three signed and sealed engineer's letters on the seawall's condition and its ability to support the proposed upland improvements. The city is confirming you are not adding load and value behind a wall that is already tired. If yours needs work, it is far better to learn that during design than after the new great room is framed and roofed.

faqs.q: Can a 1960s block ranch here carry a second story?
faqs.a: Many can, some need reinforcement, and an engineer settles it rather than a hunch. Existing block walls, tie beam and footings get evaluated, and where they fall short we design columns, new footings or an upgraded tie beam. Occasionally the honest answer is that going out toward the water serves you better than going up. Either way you get options with real numbers attached, not one take-it-or-leave-it plan.

faqs.q: How high can I actually build in Lighthouse Point?
faqs.a: Two stories, with a shape rule attached. The city's single-family districts measure height from the crown of the adjoining roadway, and any portion of the building above 28.5 feet has to pull back an extra two feet horizontally for every foot of added height. A tall second story therefore steps itself away from the property lines instead of rising straight up. Chimneys and ornamental features carry their own separate cap. We confirm your zoning district and lot conditions before anyone draws a roofline.

faqs.q: How long from first sketch to moving into the new room?
faqs.a: Plan for the front end. Design, structural engineering, survey, soil and drainage work, and permit review commonly take months before anything is dug, and construction on a substantial addition runs several more. A year from first meeting to furniture is a realistic frame, and a contractor promising dramatically less is either building something small or leaving something out. Your written schedule arrives with the estimate.

faqs.q: Should we add on or buy a bigger house on a better canal?
faqs.a: That depends on your dock more than your kitchen. Deep water, a short run out to the Hillsboro Inlet and a street you like is a combination that is hard to buy twice, and it is worth building around. If your canal is shallow, narrow, or bridged in a way that limits the boat you actually want, moving may be the better project. We will give you a candid feasibility read before you spend money on drawings.

home-additions.cta_sub: Bring the survey, the wish list and the boat dimensions if they matter. You get a candid feasibility read and honest numbers, in English o en español.

outdoor-living.title: Outdoor Living & Terraces, Lighthouse Point FL | PGX Builders
outdoor-living.meta_description: Canal-side terraces and outdoor kitchens for Lighthouse Point homes, engineered, permitted and built by a licensed GC. (786) 273-2524.
outdoor-living.h1: The good side faces the water
outdoor-living.hero_sub: Summer kitchens, covered terraces, pergolas, driveways and impact openings for Lighthouse Point waterfront homes. Engineered for HVHZ uplift, permitted through the city, and built under daily supervision by a licensed, insured general contractor.
outdoor-living.local_heading: Outdoor rooms on a dead-end canal
intro_paragraphs: In Lighthouse Point roughly eighty percent of the homes are single family and most of them front water, so the backyard is not a leftover. It is the reason people bought. Outdoor living projects here run bigger than a grill on a slab: a covered terrace and summer kitchen between the pool and the seawall in Hillsboro Isles, a pergola and fire table off a Lake Placid patio, a full redo of driveway, walkways and stucco so the street elevation stops arguing with the new interior. The dock crowd arrives by boat and stays for dinner.

Exterior work is permitted work in Lighthouse Point: patios, pool decks, fences, driveways, enclosures, generators and window or door replacements all need a permit from the city's Building and Zoning Department, and new openings need HVHZ product approvals because Broward sits inside the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone. The waterfront items live under two roofs at once. Docks, boat lifts and seawall repairs draw Broward County environmental review alongside the city permit, and the county's resiliency standards now set minimum elevations for seawalls and tidal flood barriers. Tree removal and relocation carry their own approvals as well.

We build the outside to the same standard as the inside. Summer kitchen gas, water and electrical are permitted and inspected rather than run under a patio and forgotten. Pergola footings are engineered for uplift, not guessed at. Terraces are pitched so water leaves the house instead of pooling against it. We are a general contractor, so where a project needs a licensed marine contractor for dock or seawall work, we coordinate the sequence rather than pretend it is our trade. Fixed scope, daily supervision, Lic. CGC1539072.
outdoor-living.scope_heading: What we build outside the house
outdoor-living.scope_intro: One coordinated project, whether it is a single terrace or the whole water elevation. The list below covers most Lighthouse Point backyards.

scope_items.name: Cooking on the canal side
scope_items.desc: Gas, water and power run and permitted properly, with cabinetry, counters and appliances specified for a yard fifty feet from brackish water.

scope_items.name: Covered terraces, engineered
scope_items.desc: Shade structures set on poured footings with uplift hardware sized for HVHZ, proportioned to the house instead of ordered out of a catalog.

scope_items.name: Pool decks and dockside paving
scope_items.desc: Paver and finished concrete surfaces graded to move water away from the slab, with the transition to the seawall cap detailed rather than improvised.

scope_items.name: Driveways and street elevation
scope_items.desc: New driveways, walkways, entry work, stucco repair and paint, permitted through the city and dimensioned off the survey you already have to submit.

scope_items.name: Impact doors, water side
scope_items.desc: Replacing sliders and terrace doors with HVHZ-approved impact units, flashed correctly, so the best wall in the house stops being the weakest one.

faqs.q: Do you build seawalls and docks?
faqs.a: No, and be suspicious of a general contractor who claims otherwise. Docks, lifts and seawalls are marine work with their own licensing and their own approval path, starting with Broward County environmental review before the city building department will accept a submittal. What we do is build everything landward of the seawall cap and coordinate schedules with your marine contractor, so the terrace is not poured the week their barge or crane needs the access.

faqs.q: Does a summer kitchen or pergola really need a permit?
faqs.a: Yes to both. Patios, decks, enclosures and accessory structures are permitted work in Lighthouse Point, and the gas, water and electrical runs need their own trade applications and inspections. Building without one gets you a stop work order and a penalty at twice the original fee. It is more process than a covered grill seems to warrant, and it is also why the finished thing appraises and insures as an improvement rather than a liability.

faqs.q: How do I keep an outdoor kitchen from corroding on a canal?
faqs.a: Specify once, correctly. Marine-grade stainless, powder coating rated for coastal exposure, dense stone properly sealed, hardware and fasteners chosen for salt air, and an overhang deep enough to keep driving rain off the appliances. Cabinetry merely labelled outdoor-rated rarely survives this environment for long. Getting it right the first time costs less than replacing the whole run in year four.

faqs.q: Will Broward's seawall elevation rules affect my backyard project?
faqs.a: They can, and it is worth knowing before you pour anything. Broward County adopted resiliency standards setting minimum elevations for seawalls and tidal flood barriers, phased in over the coming decades, and they generally apply when a wall is newly built or substantially repaired. If your seawall is due, raising it changes the grade of everything behind it. Far better to design the terrace once, around the final elevation, than to build it twice.

faqs.q: What should we budget for a full backyard build?
faqs.a: The number tracks structure and utility runs, not the footprint. A paver terrace and some landscape lighting is one conversation; a covered outdoor room with a summer kitchen, gas, water, power, engineered footings and new impact doors across the water elevation is genuinely another. Appliance and stone selections move the number as much as the slab does. We scope it in writing after walking the yard, so you are comparing specifications rather than guesses.

permitting-compliance.local_heading: What the address history actually says
intro_paragraphs: Half the permitting calls we take from Lighthouse Point begin with a title search. A reroof on a Venetian Isles ranch that was never signed off. A pool cage in Coral Key Villas replaced after a storm with nothing filed. A Florida room in Lighthouse Manor enclosed sometime around 1978 and still showing as a screened porch on the record. Houses here have changed hands and changed shape for sixty years, and the paperwork has not always kept pace. The rest of the calls are happier: an owner about to start something real who wants the file ahead of the work instead of chasing it later.

The permit itself is a City of Lighthouse Point matter, handled by the Building and Zoning Department through the city's online permitting portal, and contractors have to be registered with the city before they can pull one. Above that sits a layer you will never file with. The Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals is where the county's amendments to the Florida Building Code live, it certifies the plans examiners and inspectors who will handle your file, and it hears the appeal when a call needs one. Broward is High-Velocity Hurricane Zone territory, so glass, doors and roofing carry HVHZ approvals, and anything in or over the canal adds county environmental licensing.

The permit goes out under our license, CGC1539072. PGX Builders Group is a general contractor rather than a paperwork service, so accountability arrives with the signature. We read the address history before promising anything, engage the engineer, architect or surveyor a complete submittal genuinely requires, resolve plan review comments in one cycle instead of dragging the file through three, and stand on the site when the inspector arrives. Twenty-plus years of South Florida work, 150-plus remodels and additions, all of it permitted and inspected. We do not call a job finished because the punch list is. We call it finished when the city's record for your address is clear.
permitting-compliance.scope_intro: Filed ahead of a remodel or opened up years after somebody else's work, these are the five fronts that decide whether a Lighthouse Point address survives a title search.

scope_items.name: Permits left open
scope_items.desc: Every open or expired record on the address identified and sorted by what it still needs, then driven to the inspection or replacement permit that finally closes it.

scope_items.name: Legalizing what was never filed
scope_items.desc: Florida rooms enclosed decades ago, garage conversions and unrecorded window swaps documented with as-built drawings, engineered where the structure demands it, and inspected under today's code.

scope_items.name: Windows, doors and their NOAs
scope_items.desc: Openings and roofing specified to approvals that hold inside the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, with anchor details and manufacturer instructions in the submittal rather than produced afterward.

scope_items.name: Inspections met on site
scope_items.desc: Phased inspections called when the work is genuinely ready, with a supervisor present to walk the inspector through it instead of a note left on the door.

scope_items.name: Waterfront filings, in order
scope_items.desc: Dock, lift and seawall scopes sequenced so the Broward County environmental license, the city engineering permit and the building permit land in the order the city expects.

faqs.q: Title turned up an open permit from a prior owner. Now what?
faqs.a: We pull the record at Building and Zoning and read what each open item is genuinely missing. Some are waiting on nothing more than a final inspection nobody ever requested. Others need a revision, an engineer's letter, or a fresh permit because the original lapsed on its own. Where the work was never permitted at all, expect to apply after the fact and to expose enough of it for an inspector to verify. The city closes a permit by inspecting it, so begin the day it turns up.

faqs.q: Does Broward County get involved, or is this all city?
faqs.a: Both, in different ways. The permit lives with the City of Lighthouse Point, which reviews it, issues it and inspects it, and the application goes in through the city's portal. The Board of Rules and Appeals sits behind the city's building official rather than in front of the homeowner, so you never file anything there. What does take a separate county application is work in or over the waterway, a dock, a lift, a seawall, and that approval runs on its own clock.

faqs.q: Which projects in Lighthouse Point actually need a permit?
faqs.a: More than most owners assume. Cosmetic finishes such as paint, carpet and tile generally do not need one. Nearly everything else does: plumbing and electrical changes, structural openings, window and door replacement, roofing, patios, pool decks, fences, driveways, generators and accessory structures. Working without one risks a stop work order and a penalty on top of the ordinary fee, and it leaves a gap in the record that a buyer's inspector or a title search eventually finds.

faqs.q: Does the 40-year style recertification apply to my house here?
faqs.a: Not to a single-family house. Broward County requires building safety inspections on older buildings above a size threshold, administered here by the city's Building Department, and single-family homes and duplexes are exempt, which covers most of Lighthouse Point. Where it does apply, on older multi-family and commercial buildings, the obligation belongs to the association or building owner rather than an individual. Florida's milestone inspection and reserve study rules apply separately to condominium and cooperative buildings of three habitable stories or more. Repairs a report calls for are work we take on.

faqs.q: We refinance in a few weeks. Is that enough time to fix this?
faqs.a: Sometimes, and it depends entirely on what the file is short of. A permit waiting only on its final inspection can move quickly. Anything needing sealed engineering, a revision, a new survey or waterway review counts in weeks, not days, because those approvals run one after another instead of side by side. Fee schedules belong to the city and rise with the declared value of the work, so we put real numbers against your actual scope rather than guess at one here.

permitting-compliance.cta_heading: Read the file before you list
permitting-compliance.cta_sub: Tell us the address and what the title company found. We read the city file, say what is still open, and price the way out, in English o en español.
